api: vSphere Automation API (vCenter), VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0
note: This contract names every operation the client is allowed to call. The mock server serves exactly these three and nothing else.

responseBody.wire: a bare JSON string, e.g. "a1b2c3..." (quotes included) — the session token

commit.omitWhen: the caller supplied no commit, or supplied a blank one
commit.note: spec: 'if missing or null or empty the apply operation will use the latest commit'

hosts.omitWhen: the caller supplied no host list, or supplied an empty one
hosts.note: spec: 'if missing or null or empty the apply operation will remediate all hosts within the cluster'

accept_eula.note: false is a supplied value and must be sent as the JSON literal false; it is not the same as unset

responseBody.wire: a bare JSON string holding the identifier of the task that performs the remediation

queryParameters.name: spec
queryParameters.serialization: style=form + explode=true over an object: each SET property is emitted as its own top-level query parameter named after the property (return_all=..., exclude_result=...). Unset properties contribute no query parameter at all. When no property is set the request carries no query string.

properties.result: operation specific; present only when the server chooses to include it
properties.error: Vapi.Std.Errors.Error — present when status is FAILED

taskStatus.note: BLOCKED means the operation is blocked, not finished. A task may leave BLOCKED and go back to RUNNING before it settles.

asyncPattern.summary: Esx.Settings.Clusters.Software_apply$Task returns 202 with a task identifier rather than the result of the remediation. The caller polls Cis.Tasks_get with that identifier until Cis.Task.Info.status reaches a terminal value.
asyncPattern.specQuote: The result of this operation can be queried by calling the cis/tasks/{task-id} where the task-id is the response of this operation.
